findings.observation: The tracked uppercase labels, oversized serif “Running order.” headline, colored period, and explanatory line form a familiar editorial opening. On the phone, the first agenda item begins around halfway down the capture.
findings.impact: The type gives more emphasis to the page introduction than to the order the producer needs to inspect and change.
findings.repair: Compress the repeated introduction and give the agenda and its start times more of the first screen.

findings.observation: On the phone, each duration sits in small muted text directly beneath an equally small category label.
findings.impact: The duration is harder to distinguish from secondary metadata, although it explains the changing start times.
findings.repair: Give durations a clearer type role or place them consistently beside the corresponding time or item name.

findings.observation: In the drag capture, “RELEASE HERE” is extremely faint and partly covered by the held row.
findings.impact: The text does little to identify the prospective slot while the producer is deciding where to drop the item.
findings.repair: Keep the slot label visible outside the held row and raise its contrast.

strengths: The agenda rows pair prominent start times with clear item names, making the settled order easy to scan.
The reordered capture shows “Field notes” at 18:25 and confirms the move and new time in plain language.
The serif time numerals give the schedule a distinct voice without obscuring the item names.
limits: Still captures cannot verify motion, keyboard behavior, focus, or whether the apparent settled row is a transition frame.
Font files and computed type settings were not available from the captures.

findings.observation: In the reordered capture, the third row still sits partly over the footer, with a visible gap and guide lines above it.
findings.impact: The settled result looks unfinished, and the row obscures part of the programme end area.
findings.repair: Remove the drag placeholder and settle the third row inside the list before showing the completed state. Recheck the reordered capture at the same size.

findings.observation: In the drag capture, the prospective slot’s “RELEASE HERE” label is extremely faint and partly covered by the held row.
findings.impact: The producer cannot clearly tell where the item will land.
findings.repair: Place a high contrast target cue in the exposed part of the slot, then recheck it while the row is held over the final position.

strengths: The default desktop and phone layouts make the agenda, start times, durations, reset action, and local sample status easy to find.
The reordered capture preserves item identities and durations and shows the expected start times: 18:00, 18:10, and 18:25. Its confirmation names the moved item and new time.
The restrained palette and clear type hierarchy suit a small event planning tool.
limits: Static captures cannot verify touch or keyboard reordering, focus, reset behavior, cancelled or rapid drags, resize, or reduced motion.
No playback of the named motion reference was supplied, so fidelity to its movement cannot be judged.
